newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - API stock-draw data seen mildly supportive.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - API stock-draw data seen mildly supportive.

text.p: Solid draws on U.S. refined products reported late Tuesday by the American Petroleum Institute were deemed mildly supportive, helping nudge futures prices higher in after-hours ACCESS trade, traders said.
The API report for the week ending April 18 showed a 4.7 million barrel draw on distillates, defying market expectations of a half-million barrel decline.

Among the distillates, low sulfur diesel declined by 3.0 million barrels, although total stocks were 5.8 million higher than the same week last year. And heating oil shrank by 1.07 million, to about 2.2 million above last year.

"But the distillate draw will probably only be marginally supportive on East Coast differentials because they've already been bid up" on tight supplies, one trader said, although he predicted futures players "will buy on the statistics."
Traders said the most surprising element in the report was a 3.1-million-barrel downward revision in total U.S. gasoline stocks for the prior April 11 API report.

"That's a very big correction," said senior analyst Ken Miller of Houston consulting firm Pervin & Gertz, who noted the API had estimated a puzzling 3.6 million barrel build despite a marked decline in gasoline production that week.
"It shot up for no apparent reason," he said, adding that the correction was almost entirely for East Coast gasoline stocks, which had showed a 3.4 million barrel build for the week of April 11.
By contrast, he said the new report shows a "more seasonal" gasoline draw of 1.9 million barrels for the week of April 19, putting total stocks about 8.9 million below this time last year.
Tom Knight, a senior trader for Fina Inc, said he has been bewildered by widely shifting API implied demand figures for gasoline recently.

"It's 8.2 million barrels one week, then 7.1 million, and now 8.4 million. You have to take them with a grain of salt," he said, but added that this week's estimates are both positive for gasoline and distillates.
The latest API data peg the refinery utilization rate at 93.5 percent, a shade lower than the 93.6 percent seen the prior week.
Overall gasoline production, it showed, rose by 337,000 barrels per day over the prior week, reaching 7.7 million barrels per day.
